programmes.t: Xploration Outer Space S4 - "Landing on Mars"
programmes.d: Host Emily Calandrelli looks at the varied and ingenious methods used to land spacecraft on the red planet, starting with Pathfinder in 1997.

programmes.t: Secrets of the Factories S1 - "Secrets of Kellogg's Cereals"
programmes.d: In Kellogg’s first factory in Europe, built in the 1930s in Trafford Park, Manchester, we meet the people who flake the corn and puff the rice, the tasters who test, and the robots and hi-tech machines that help keep the boxes rolling out day and night.

programmes.t: Science of Thrills S1 - "Speed"
programmes.d: Engineer and adventurer Rob Bell climbs aboard some of the world’s fastest theme park rides and learns what it takes to build them.

programmes.t: Science of Thrills S1 - "Falling"
programmes.d: Engineer and adventurer Rob Bell discovers how our fear of falling is exploited by some of the world’s top theme park rides.

programmes.t: Science of Thrills S1 - "Height"
programmes.d: Engineer and adventurer Rob Bell climbs aboard four spectacular rollercoasters in Europe and America that exploit our fear of heights.

programmes.t: Science of Thrills S1 - "Inversion"
programmes.d: Engineer and adventurer Rob Bell investigates four roller coasters in Europe and America that use inversions, or loops, to create thrilling rides.

programmes.t: How Things Work S1 - "Chainsaws, Jukeboxes, and Fishing Reels"
programmes.d: Chainsaw, jukebox, fishing reel, car wash, blender and bicycle pump... Using ultra realistic CGI animation, we explode everyday objects into their component parts, to reveal their secret workings.

programmes.t: How Things Work S1 - "Escalators, Leaf Blowers, and Music Boxes"
programmes.d: Escalator, leaf blower, tape measure, security safe, tennis ball launcher, music box... Using ultra realistic CGI animation, we explode everyday objects into their component parts, to reveal their secret workings.

programmes.t: Angry Planet S3 - "Polynesian Volcanoes"
programmes.d: Filming the volcanoes, mudpools and geysers in the geothermic wonderland of New Zealand’s north island, we learn that a new island is being created by an undersea volcano 1000 miles north in Tonga

programmes.t: Angry Planet S3 - "Highway to Hell"
programmes.d: George heads straight into the “Bearcage”, looking to get beat up by the biggest, baddest hailstones that Texas and Oklahoma can throw at them. He finds it –and the stormchasing vehicles don’t look too pretty after coming through these massive storms

programmes.t: Angry Planet S3 - "Space"
programmes.d: We break the bounds of earth, and look at the environment of space. We examine the difficulties and challenges of exploring this most challenging environment.

programmes.t: Exceptional Engineering S1 - "Emergency Helicopter"
programmes.d: In Bavaria, engineers build the high-tech H145 rescue helicopter, while skilled pilots navigate extreme terrain to save lives.

programmes.t: Exceptional Engineering S1 - "Harvesting Giants"
programmes.d: Inside the Fendt factory, advanced GPS technology and complex assembly lines create the world's most powerful 517-hp agricultural tractor.

programmes.t: Bridging the Expanse S1 - "The Elegance of Iron"
programmes.d: Industrial Revolution innovations in iron, steel, and railway construction spawn truss and suspension designs capable of spanning vast divides.

programmes.t: Wonder S1 - "Color"
programmes.d: In this episode we'll understand how chromatic adaptation works, how do we see the color pink and why do blue rarely exists in nature.

programmes.t: Wonder S1 - "Problems"
programmes.d: A lot of problems in this episode. What is the Birthday Problem? Why the Gambler's Ruin debunks the 'luck' factor? And is the union of two sets with infinite elements still be infinity?

programmes.t: Strange World S1 - "Ice Bombs"
programmes.d: Alex heads to America search of a scientific explanation for the terrifying phenomenon known as Ice Bombs, which cause fear, devastation and even injury.

programmes.t: Strange World S1 - "Alien Sounds"
programmes.d: Mysterious, alien sky sounds terrify Canadian residents, who struggle to locate their source.

programmes.t: Quick Connections with Alie Ward S1 - "Living Virtually"
programmes.d: How did the invention of photography lead us to a world where we live entirely virtually? Alie Ward will point us towards a future where we might upload ourselves to the web.

programmes.t: Power & S3 - "Kapap - Amit Himelstein"
programmes.d: Amit Himelstein is the head instructor of the IKF and the leader in Kapap. His big motto? Respect everyone but fear no-one. He’s the embodiment of krav maga.

programmes.t: Razor: Science For a Better Future S1 - "Imaging the Aurora"
programmes.d: Reya El-Salahi explores how the northern lights can disrupt technology and visits EISCAT 3D, a new radar studying solar particle impacts.

programmes.t: Razor: Science For a Better Future S1 - "Long COVID"
programmes.d: Emma meets Dr. Asad Khan, whose life was upended by long COVID, as new research seeks answers for millions still suffering worldwide.

programmes.t: Razor: Science For a Better Future S1 - "Rewilding Bison"
programmes.d: Emma Keeling treks through Romania’s Tarcu Mountains to see how European bison, once extinct in the wild, are making a comeback.

programmes.t: Razor: Science For a Better Future S1 - ""The Way" to Fusion"
programmes.d: Neil Cairns visits ITER in France, where nuclear fusion could provide unlimited clean energy, to see progress and challenges firsthand.

programmes.t: Razor: Science For a Better Future S1 - "Urban Microbiome"
programmes.d: Research shows sanitized cities reduce beneficial microbes, harming health and increasing allergies and autoimmune diseases.

programmes.t: Future Warfare S1 - "Artificial Intelligence & Autonomy"
programmes.d: As military algorithms outpace human capability, experts explore the risks and ethical choices of deploying fully autonomous weapon systems.

programmes.t: Future Warfare S1 - "Cyber Warfare"
programmes.d: Virtual attacks replace traditional battlefields, showing how hackers target critical infrastructure, data, and governments without physical force.

programmes.t: Made in Britain S1 - "Whitaker's Chocolates and Heck! Sausages"
programmes.d: Lord Prescott visits Whitaker’s chocolate factory to explore large-scale chocolate making, from factory lines to expert tasting and the company’s rich history. He then heads to HECK! Sausages in North Yorkshire, where he attempts to create his own custom recipe—the Hull banger.

programmes.t: Made in Britain S1 - "Wensleydale Cheese and Mowbray Pork Pies"
programmes.d: At the Wensleydale Creamery, Lord Prescott joins master cheesemakers to follow the production of the famous Yorkshire Wensleydale cheese, learning the art of cheese-tasting along the way. His next stop is Mowbray Pork Pies, where he experiences the high-speed world of pie production.

programmes.t: Made in Britain S1 - "Lea and Perrins Worcestershire Sauce and Soreen's Malt Loaf"
programmes.d: Exploring the historic Lea & Perrins factory, Lord Prescott uncovers the story behind its legendary Worcestershire sauce, made since 1837. He then heads to Manchester to the Soreen factory, home of the beloved malt loaf, where he joins the production line and experiments with creating a new flavour.

programmes.t: Made in Britain S1 - "Ambrosia's desserts and Young's battered fish"
programmes.d: To discover how his favourite meal—fish supper followed by rice pudding—is made, Lord Prescott visits the Ambrosia factory in Devon to explore the production of classic British desserts. Returning north to Grimsby, he heads to the Young's factory to learn about their famous fish pie.

programmes.t: Made in Britain S1 - "Typhoo Tea and Fox's biscuits"
programmes.d: In search of the classic British pairing, tea and biscuits, Lord Prescott travels to Liverpool to visit the Typhoo tea factory, discovering the key to a perfectly brewed cup. Back in Yorkshire, he stops by the Fox’s biscuits factory, rounding off his journey with a truly British treat.
